clue.text: Work's been mounted, look … as sport

indicators.note: in a down clue, something mounted is set upright, so the word for work reads from bottom to top

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
LO is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone's artwork has been framed and hung, and a viewer is told to look at it as sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work's been mounted' reads as an artwork hung on a wall; in a down clue, 'been mounted' means the piece is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a team game played on horseback, so it is one kind of sport.

indicators.note: a windy day blows things about, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has tied on their hat because it is a blustery day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy' rearranges HAT and BEING into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a result that is in the bag is certain or already secured.

clue.text: Made an impression and got fellow going

indicators.note: the abbreviation for fellow goes away, leaving the rest of the word for got

parts.note: to go and get something is to fetch it, so got gives fetched

explanation.surface: Someone impressed people and then sent a friend on his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' takes F out of FETCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Etching cuts lines into a surface, literally making an impression in it.

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of temper, and one had while driving along the road is the motorist's rage

explanation.surface: A man called Paddy seems to be travelling somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy reads as a name, but in British slang a paddy is a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is a temper tantrum, and one thrown by a driver on the road is this phenomenon.

clue.text: Take great delight over one in show

indicators.note: the word for taking great delight sits over, covering, the letter for one

parts.note: to revel is to take great delight
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly enjoys a single act in a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts REVEL around A.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show it, making it visible or known.

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being thrown into confusion, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A person stays red-faced for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassed' rearranges ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are immensely long periods of time, informally ages.

clue.text: Works of Shakespeare special (none played to empty theatres)

indicators.note: the letters of none are played about with, moved into a fresh arrangement
an empty theatre keeps only its walls, so just the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A special production of Shakespeare's works was staged to no audience at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' turns NONE into ONNE, and 'empty' leaves TS of theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote 154 sonnets, fourteen-line poems, so they are among his works.

clue.text: Is aware of discussing one patient's operation

indicators.note: discussing means speaking, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: someone who is aware of something knows it
Job in the Bible is the byword for patience, a patient one

explanation.surface: Someone is aware of what is being said about a patient's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discussing' turns KNOWS into its sound twin NOSE. The patience of Job is a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty, the cosmetic reshaping of the nose, is a surgical operation.

clue.text: Rubbish! Best to leave quietly and say nothing

indicators.note: the musical letter for quietly is told to leave the word for best

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly
sh is the sound used to tell someone to say nothing

explanation.surface: Someone is advised to slip away quietly and keep their mouth shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes P from TOP, leaving TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for nonsense, an exclamation like rubbish.

indicators.note: something worn down is broken and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is afraid of having to put on a tiara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' rearranges SHE DREADS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornament worn on the head, an example of the general term.

parts.note: Roads sounds like Rhodes, a Greek island found here on the main, an old word for the sea

explanation.surface: A remark about where road noise is mostly heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roads' is said like Rhodes, and 'mainly' hints at the main, poetic for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek island of Rhodes lies in this stretch of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Artwork (some say) made by man? Not entirely in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back means the run of letters is read from right to left
only part of the words is used, a run of letters lifted from inside them

explanation.surface: A question whether a work of art could have been made by a man, rethought in hindsight.
explanation.walkthrough: The run DEBYM sits within 'made by man' ('Not entirely') and 'in retrospect' reverses it. '(some say)' notes not everyone calls it art.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey Emin's installation of her unmade bed is a famous and divisive work of art.

indicators.note: the letter for kelvin is placed in the word for bar

parts.note: a Mars is a well-known chocolate bar
K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: A man named Kelvin is greeted when he walks into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mars bar is a chocolate bar sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to notice or recognise it, as in marking an anniversary.

indicators.note: the letters take on a new form, being rearranged

explanation.surface: A task becomes harder when it is presented on a bigger scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges LARGER and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarly is slang for tricky or awkward, so the comparative means trickier.

indicators.note: the letters are taken in, held within the words when and Rolf

explanation.surface: Someone is let in once Rolf has been brought inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol someone is to admit them as a member of a course or society.

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
rag is a dismissive word for a tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone's deception is exposed by a popular newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' reads as deceit, but it is a steep cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff or headland, and a crag is a steep rugged rock face.

clue.text: Try to take off, but freak out

parts.note: to have a go is to try
to ape someone is to take them off, to mimic them

explanation.surface: A plane attempts to get airborne and the passenger panics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like flight; it means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to go wild with rage or excitement is to lose control, to freak out.

indicators.note: turned round, the word for whip reads backwards

parts.note: to flog is to whip
a club is a group or society

explanation.surface: A collection is taken by a society to pay for its chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' looks like a collection of money, but it splits into whip and the reversal signal 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is the long-hitting club a golfer uses off the tee.

parts.note: to stand for someone is to represent them

explanation.surface: Someone acts on behalf of shopping centres in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Fora is a plural of forum, the marketplace of an ancient Roman town.

clue.text: Light hit lover with force on head

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter for force sits on the head of the other pieces

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
to lam is to hit hard
a beau is a boyfriend or lover

explanation.surface: Someone struck their partner forcefully on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective (hit lightly) but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, a source of light.

clue.text: Attacks with a 'furious fastidiousness', ultimately — fine to ignore flaws

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the three words
the letter for fine is ignored, left out of the word for flaws

parts.note: faults are flaws
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A critic's assaults show such obsessive fussiness that small flaws should be overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' drops F from FAULTS, leaving AULTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaults are violent attacks, used here as a plural noun.

clue.text: Judge, after tip-off, goes by — heading for Specsavers?

indicators.note: with its tip taken off, the word for goes by loses its first letter

parts.note: passes means goes by

indicators.note: the heading of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A judge, after a tip-off, walks past on the way to an optician's chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after tip-off' drops P from PASSES. Specsavers is a British chain of opticians.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to evaluate or judge it.

indicators.note: the word for individual leaves the surname of Sly

parts.note: Sylvester Stallone is known as Sly
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A crafty person walks out of a market stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sly' looks like 'crafty' but is the actor Sylvester Stallone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stall is a stand from which goods are sold at a market.

clue.text: Model gets disheartened over artist's range

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the second
the heart of the word for model, its two middle letters, is removed

parts.note: a sitter is a model posing for a portrait
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A model is downcast about a painter's collection of works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes TT from SITTER, leaving SIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged mountain range, as in the Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Show active disrespect for one poor critic's conclusions — teased outrageously

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled
the conclusions of the words are their final letters

explanation.surface: A bad reviewer's verdicts mock someone cruelly and disrespectfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusions' takes E, R and C from one, poor and critic('s is ignored); 'outrageously' mixes them with TEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: To desecrate is to violate something sacred, an act of active disrespect.

definitions.meaning: a legislative assembly, as in Japan's national parliament
a restricted eating plan, cutting how much food is eaten

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an assembly like the German Diet and a regime of restricted eating.

parts.note: bar means except, as does but

indicators.note: the letter in front of the word is its first

explanation.surface: Someone halts, though still in the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar is to block or prevent, so it stops something happening.

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a judge tries a case, or hears it

explanation.surface: Advice to someone who cannot fly: get on a bike instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the R of HEAR to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird, like an ostrich.

clue.text: Is sure to be injured — athlete's back put out again

indicators.note: injured letters are damaged and set out in a new order
the back of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An athlete is certain to get hurt, and their back is put out once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be injured' rearranges IS SURE; 'back' gives E, the last letter of athlete ('s ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue is to publish or release something again, so it is put out a second time.

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: fanciful means imaginative, so these letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie looks at paintings with imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancifully' rearranges SEE ART.
explanation.definitionFit: To create is to make or bring something into being.
